And addressed as 'Son, son!' by the wise Śarva, / Brahmā bowed with folded hands and went to him alone for refuge. / Bestowing upon Brahmā the role of creator together with knowledge, / and the sovereignty of the worlds, the Supreme Lord disappeared.
Therefore this eternal Upaniṣad has been spoken by me, O Vyāsa, / hearing which yogins, through meditation, take refuge in Maheśvara:
'He who appointed Brahmā as son in the beginning, and who sent knowledge to him— / the wise who see Him abiding in the self, theirs is eternal peace, not others'.' / Having seen his father endowed with supreme radiance, O Vyāsa,
desiring a son, for the sake of offspring he performed fierce austerity. / To him, the great-souled one endowed with fierce yoga and austerity, / in a short time indeed his father became well pleased. / And he came into his view and said, 'I grant a boon.'

Thus indeed this goddess, proceeding to the realm of Brahmā, / turned away from the middle of the sacrificial altar for the sake of the fulfillment of your dharma.
Sanatkumāra said:
Thus when their thousand-year sacrifice was concluded, / and when the Sarasvatī was flowing, the Grandfather arrived there.

Again worship the divine Lord here with this sacrifice. / When there will be an obstacle for you, then your austerity will be free of taint.

Then all those seers, their sins burned away by austerity, / praised Gāyatrī, who brings forth the Vedas, with desired hymns.
As they were praising her, Gāyatrī, who brings forth the Vedas, / granted them darśana in embodied form and spoke thus to those twice-born:
"I am pleased, my children! What shall I do for you today? I grant you boons. / Speak, and it shall be done this very day; there is no doubt."
The seers said:
"O goddess, our Soma has been carried off by some evil person. / Bring him back! Homage to you; this is our supreme boon."
Sanatkumāra said:
Thus addressed, having ascertained [the place] and seen with her divine eye, / she took the form of a hawk and flew swiftly toward the asura Svarbhānu.
Taking the Soma from the bewildered asuras, she returned. / Arriving, she said to those seers: "Let this Soma be pressed!"
Having obtained him, the seers, securing the great fruit of the sacrifice, / considered their austerity to be spotless, O twice-born.

The yogins, disciplined in the application of austerity, bowing to Bhava who is pure as the moon, / having received their sight in the sky from the Lord, were filled with joy along with the gods.

Thus ends the eighth chapter, named The Vision of Rudra, in the Skandapurāṇa.
Sanatkumāra said:
Having seen the Lord of the God of gods, the gods headed by Brahmā and Indra / bowed down to the rider of the bull and praised him with desired words.

"Homage to Śiva, to Soma, who removes the fear of devotees! / Homage to him whose hand holds the tip of the trident, and who carries a water-pot!
Homage to you, blue-throated one, with terrifying fangs, / whose eyes blaze like the three sacrificial fires, three-eyed one, and Hara!
Homage to the bearer of Pināka, and homage to the wielder of the thunderbolt, / to him whose sacred thread is a serpent, and whose ornament is ear-rings. (4)

Sanatkumāra said:
Once Himavān asked a question of Kaśyapa, the best of two-footed beings, who had arrived at his house: / "What, pray, brings renown in the world? / By what, O sage, do worlds become imperishable and renown supreme, / and likewise venerability among the good? Tell me that!"
Kaśyapa said:
"All this is obtained through offspring, O fortunate one! / My renown is through offspring, and so is Brahmā's together with the seers. / Do you not see it, O king of mountains, that you question me? / I shall also relate what was seen by me long ago, O mountain.

7.1.m:
Going to Vārāṇasī, I saw standing in the sky / an aerial chariot, resounding, divine, matchless, and unblemished. / Beneath it, I heard a cry of distress in a pit: / […]
Having known them by austerity, I stood right there, concealed. / Then, O king of mountains, a brahmin arrived there, restrained in vows, pure, / his soul purified by bathing in sacred fords, devoted to supreme austerity.
Then, as he was walking, the twice-born, terrified by a tiger, / entered that place where that pit was, O mountain. / In the pit, he then saw sages hanging from a clump of vīraṇa grass; / afflicted, he saw them afflicted with sorrow, and that twice-born questioned them:
'Who are you, hanging head downwards from a clump of vīraṇa grass, / distressed? By what will your release come to pass, O sinless ones?'"
